## Further Reading

Dasu, T., & Johnson, T. (2003). *Exploratory data mining and data cleaning*. Wiley. <https://doi.org/10.1002/0471448354> A book-length treatment of data quality, data cleaning, and the exploratory analysis that should precede any formal analysis. It is written for analysts who work with large, imperfect databases and is a good next step for readers who want to go beyond spreadsheet techniques.

Fernandes, A. A. A., Koehler, M., Konstantinou, N., Pankin, P., Paton, N. W., & Sakellariou, R. (2023). Data preparation: A technological perspective and review. *SN Computer Science*, *4*(4), Article 425. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s42979-023-01828-8> This open-access review describes the activities at the heart of data preparation, profiling, matching, mapping, format transformation, and data repair, and shows how they appear in programming, workflow, and table-based tools. It places the Excel and Power Query techniques of this chapter within the wider field.

Gantman, S., & Metzger, L. (2022). Vendor master data cleaning: A project for accounting class. *Journal of Emerging Technologies in Accounting*, *19*(1), 165–171. <https://doi.org/10.2308/jeta-2020-028> This teaching case sets a project to plan, carry out, and report on the cleaning of a large set of real vendor master data. It complements Exercise 5.6 by showing the planning, testing, and communication that a full data cleaning project requires.

Hunter, K., Alberti, C. T., Boss, S. R., & Thibodeau, J. C. (2020). IntelliClean: A teaching case designed to integrate data cleaning and spreadsheet skills into the audit curriculum. *Journal of Emerging Technologies in Accounting*, *17*(2), 17–24. <https://doi.org/10.2308/jeta-2020-025> Written for auditing courses, this case works through cleaning a data set in a spreadsheet and verifying its completeness and accuracy in accordance with auditing standards. It shows how the preparation checks in this chapter become audit evidence.

Lee, L. S., Casterella, G., & Wray, B. (2021). Preparing for audit data analytics with the AICPA general ledger audit data standards. *Journal of Emerging Technologies in Accounting*, *18*(1), 131–157. <https://doi.org/10.2308/jeta-2020-022> This exercise cleanses and transforms non-standardized client ledger data so that it conforms to the AICPA's Audit Data Standards, and then tests it. It explains why standard data formats reduce the preparation burden on auditors.

Microsoft. (2026). *Merge queries overview*. Microsoft Learn. <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/merge-queries-overview> Microsoft's reference for the Merge Queries command, which describes how to choose the key columns, how to expand the merged column, and each join kind, with links to worked examples of every kind. It also introduces fuzzy matching, which finds approximate matches between text columns.

Rahm, E., & Do, H. H. (2000). Data cleaning: Problems and current approaches. *IEEE Data Engineering Bulletin*, *23*(4), 3–13. <http://sites.computer.org/debull/A00dec/A00DEC-CD.pdf> A widely cited classification of the data quality problems that data cleaning addresses, distinguishing problems within a single source from those that arise when sources are integrated. Its point that cleaning is most needed when combining heterogeneous sources applies directly to building a table such as InvoiceLines.
